intro.title: Peridot Stone
intro.description: Peridot's unique color and purity makes it a popular semi-precious gemstone. During the Middle Ages, Peridot was a very sought-after gemstone, it is believed that a Peridot stone was the prized possession of Queen Cleopatra. The first discoveries of peridot are said to have been made 3000 years ago on the island of Zebirget, in the Red Sea. Greenstone Peridot has been made into jewelry and worn since it was first discovered.

tabs.tab1_description:
Peridot gemstone is a lovely shimmering Olive Green gemstone which comes in only various shades of Green color and is said to glow in the dark if slight light falls on them. The most common one is the Yellowish-Green Peridot gem, though its colors have variations from Olive to dark Green Peridot. Interestingly this natural gemstone is called Olivine gemstone, surely borrowing this name from the mineral Olivine which forms it and which has the chemical composition of Magnesium-Iron silicate, with the iron content lending the Peridot gem its Green hue, so the intensity of the Green color increases if there is more iron content. The name Peridot is said to have been derived from the Greek word "Peridona", which roughly means "giving plenty". Also the name Peridot is very similar to the Arabian 'Feridaat' which translated, means 'gem'. Peridot stone in Hindi is called Kalbindu Harit.

Peridot gemstone was first mined in the Topaz Island, now known as Zabargad or St. John's Island in the Egyptian Red Sea. Inspired by the beautiful color, the ancient Egyptians used to call Peridot stone "Gem of the Sun". A rich contemporary source of this Gemstone is the Himalayas. In hardness, it measures 6.5 on Mohs scale. Unlike other gemstones, this natural stone is formed in the molten rocks much deeper in the Earth's upper mantle and is brought up by volcanic eruptions or tectonic shifts.

Peridot has the capability to regenerate physically and give rejuvenating energies to the mind. Aids in moving ahead in life leaving past wounds behind by healing the ego. Among the Peridot properties, a practical and remarkable point is that this mystical stone can help to find lost or misplaced objects.

It is said that by holding the Peridot stone either in hand or some suggest putting it on the forehead to recollect and get back the objects of the material world along with that Peridot stone benefits in the quest to the spiritual journey. Peridot properties have an important contribution to healing relationships, fortifying it, and helps to understand one's purpose in life.

In Vedic Astrology, peridot is considered to be a substitute for Emerald gemstone. Peridot has been long famous for its mystic and healing properties. It was believed that peridot provides protection and helps heals liver diseases. Pirates prized it for its ability to ward off the terrors of the night.

Hailing from the deeper layers of Earth, peridot metaphysical properties include regeneration which is an important part of peridot stone. Though very rarely, peridot in meteorites is also found and termed pallasite peridot.

tabs.tab2_description:
Although Peridot gemstone can be worn by anyone for its healing, mystic and other benefits, it is highly recommended that an astro and chakra expert consultation is sought before wearing Peridot. In Chakra science, it helps open and balance the Heart and the Heart Chakra. Thus, it is highly recommended for those looking for relief from stress, peace of mind and calmness.

One may also consult a Chakra analyst or a Vedic astrologer to check the compatibility of the stone. This gemstone blesses with a feeling of soothing and relaxing effect. You can take advantage of our expert advice on the suitability and compatibility of wearing this stone.

Those who lack logic, rational thought, and a positive outlook should wear a Peridot to counteract Mercury's negative effects. Wearing this sparkling gemstone can help those who are stuck in emotional traumas from relationships.

Peridot blesses its wearer with cordial relationships, understanding and contentment.

Important Details:

Note that one should only wear natural, unheated, untreated Peridot gemstones so they can experience healing and empowerment. Rudra Centre only deals in 100% natural, unheated, untreated Peridot gemstones.

Peridot Buying Guide

Check its Origin:

Peridot is the national gemstone of Egypt. The Burmese Peridot, from Burma is of the finest quality of Peridot gem, Arizona and New Mexico are significant commercial Peridot producers, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Saudi Arabia, China, Egypt, South Africa, Tanzania, Australia and India are other Peridot miners. A rich contemporary source is the Himalayas.

Observe their Color:

The color spectrum of peridot ranges from pristine green to yellowish green to greenish yellow. The finest shade of green has no yellow or brown undertones. Above 10 carats, the gem's colors are typically at their finest. The color of inferior peridot is brownish. Pure green gemstones are uncommon, and the majority of peridots are yellowish green. The stones of superior quality have an intense hue. Myanmar and Pakistan produce the majority of the finest-colored stones.

Notice their Clarity:

Peridot of the finest quality has a medium-toned, intensely saturated, yellowish-green hue and a sparkling clarity.

Examine their Inclusions:

Under magnification, the finest-quality peridot contains no inclusions that are visible to the naked eye, with the exception of a few minute black spots, which are actually minute mineral crystals. Other common inclusions in peridot consist of reflective, disk-shaped inclusions known as "lily pads." The value of peridot is diminished by easily discernible inclusions, particularly dark areas. The value of light-colored materials with prominent dark inclusions decreases dramatically.

See their Shape:

Peridot can be a stunning gem if its beautiful body color is enhanced by skilled cutting. It is available in numerous shapes and cuts, including ovals, pears, rounds, emerald cuts, cushion cuts, triangle cuts, and marquise shapes.

Check the Carats:

For Peridot of gem quality, the raw Peridot is divided and polished into smaller stones of variable carat weight. In general, Peridot weighing between 5 and 7 carats are appropriate for jewelry. Because Peridot is sold by weight, Peridot prices are calculated per carat. Stones of comparable dimensions but distinct varieties vary greatly in price. The more carats and clarity Peridot has, the higher its price.

Avoid Heated & Treated Peridot:

Due to treatments the Peridot stone loses its natural composition and thus loses its natural frequency. These heated and treated Peridot do not offer any healing benefits and should be avoided.

Check for Lab Certificate:

It is recommended that you should purchase Peridot gemstones along a lab tested certificate which can determine its authenticity, treatment status and origin. Rudra Centre has been dealing in natural unheated untreated lab certified gemstones for the past 25 years. Our Peridot are certified from trusted labs like GIA, IGI, GLI and IGITL.

Why buy Peridot from Rudra Centre?

We only deal with untreated and unheated gemstones from their natural sources, which we energize in accordance with Vedic Vidhi, after more than 20 years of research and 100.000+ satisfied, healed, and empowered customers.

Can I give my used Peridot gemstone to someone else?

You should avoid it if you are wearing it. However, if you have not used it for an extended period, you can pass it on to someone else. It is recommended to not wear it for at least 2 weeks before giving it to someone else. You can also follow the cleansing and reenergizing process mentioned in the benefits section.

If after a few days of wearing you feel completely energized, inspired, and normal instead of confused, drowsy and numb, Peridot is a good choice for you. tabs.tab4_description:
For the best results it is highly recommended that one wears only 100% natural, unheated, and untreated Peridot gemstones. As per the Vedic scriptures, a heat treatment harms its sattvic nature, rendering the stone less effective and beneficial. Like other gemstones, the quality of Peridot is also determined by the four Cs (Color, Cut, Carat, Clarity).

Color

The best quality peridot are bottle green in color with vivid and vibrant color saturation and tone that is not too dark or light. The color should be evenly distributed with no visible color-zone. The shiniest the color the highest its value.

Cut

Best quality peridot have cuts that maximize the effect of hue, tone, saturation and surface area.

Carat

Peridot of 5 – 7 carat is most popular in Vedic Astrology. Significant smaller and larger peridots are used in contemporary jewelry. Generally, the price of Peridot rises as the size/weight/carat increases.

Clarity

Peridot typically contains some inclusions, but the best-quality peridot has no eye-visible inclusions. The tiny inclusions can only be seen under magnification.

Dealers deal in peridot which are synthetic to natural but which are treated/heated and color enhanced, so it is immensely important to purchase only from a reputed dealer with certification from a reputed lab.

Peridot gemstone Price

The price of Peridot gemstone depends on its size, its cut, as well as its origin in terms of color and clarity. Stones of exceptional quality can be more expensive, and the larger the carat weight, the higher the price per carat. As stated previously, stones from Myanmar and Pakistan are typically more expensive than those from other countries.

Frequently, the cost of a peridot is substantially increased by the jewelry setting in which it is mounted. Observe the price difference between a peridot of good quality and a peridot of heirloom quality. The difference in price is over 1000 USD.

When a gemstone is heat-treated or undergoes the dying process, its healing properties are lost when it is worn. Peridot has numerous curative properties; to maximize its curative effects, only untreated Peridot stone should be worn.

The price of genuine, natural and unheated, untreated Peridot gemstones at Rudra Centre ranges from INR 4,640 to INR 13,200 (USD 58 to USD 165).

How to Identify or Test Original & Authentic Peridot?

The best way to check the authenticity of Peridot is by getting a Lab tested report from a reputed laboratory. Rudra Centre only deals with Vedic Astrology approved gemstones that are natural, untreated, and unheated. All our Peridot are certified by reputable labs like GIA, GLI, IGI and IGITL.

Look for flaws along with inclusions. Use a magnifying glass with at least 10x magnification to examine the Peridot carefully. Look for specks and blemishes, as they form with minute particles of other material. These flaws are strong evidence that a Peridot is genuine. Lab-created (fake) Peridot have no inclusions of this nature, and neither do natural Peridot, but if you find flaws, then your Peridot is genuine.

Examine the gemstone for air bubbles. Essentially, lab-created Peridot are glass that has undergone a process similar to that which forms natural Peridot. Since they are made of glass, they retain miniscule air bubbles after formation. If there are bubbles within the Peridot, it is not genuine. Be sure to inspect your Peridot from every angle by turning it over. There is a possibility that bubbles of air will only be evident from a single angle.

Look at how light is reflected by the Peridot. Turn off all the lights and shine your flashlight on the Peridot. If it is genuine, it will only reflect light of the same hue as itself. If it is a fake, made of glass, it will reflect colors other than the natural color of the gem.

Peridot Cleaning & Maintenance

It is essential to give your gemstone a thorough cleaning in order to preserve its luster, as regular use can cause it to become dull. This washing enables it to purge itself from negative energies as well.

Peridot is resistant to light but vulnerable to sulfuric acid and less so to hydrochloric acid. It is also vulnerable to long-term acidic perspiration attack. Warm, soapy water is the best peridot cleaning solution. It is not recommended to use ultrasonic or steam cleaners.
